text:
Alice M: Heads up — since the routing-policy rollout at ~09:10 we've seen exporter CPU climb and p99 tail latency for inference routes creep up. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/inference/telemetry — can anyone take a look? :eyes:
Ben R: I noticed the collector pod on telemetry-prod-2 went to 85% CPU around the same time, queue length for otlp_exporter spiked to ~15k :grimacing:
Carmen S: Confirming. The OTEL collector change bumped exporter worker threads and removed batching cap in the new config. Suspect batching blowup -> more small sends -> higher syscalls.
Dinesh: Sharing logs from exporter: 
```
2026-02-10T09:11:22Z exporter.go:237 send_batch size=16 num_bytes=12000 took=2.3ms
2026-02-10T09:11:22Z exporter.go:238 send_batch size=3 num_bytes=800 took=4.8ms
2026-02-10T09:12:00Z queue.go:85 queue_len=15234
```
Eva L: Quick note — compression helps network but can cost CPU. We recently flipped on gzip for otlp; that could explain part of CPU lift.
Ben R: Right. In our perf testing gzip on arm64 added ~25% CPU at 50 rps; snappy was ~5% but less compression.
Carmen S: Proposed mitigation: restore batching cap, lower exporter concurrency, and enable backoff. Also consider per-route sampling to stop instrumenting very chatty internal spans (kv-cache debug spans).
Alice M: Can you paste the config diff you suspect? Want to try rolling to a single collector replica with old config in canary.
Carmen S: Here's the relevant fragment we changed: 
```
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "otlp.internal:4317"
    compression: gzip
    retry_on_failure:
      enabled: true
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 512
    timeout: 10s
extensions:
  health_check: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [otlp]
```
We removed a static queue_size and bumped send_batch_size in the later commit.
Dinesh: If send_batch_size is too big, we actually wait more for batches then flush many small ones when the timeout hits — but more likely the removal of queue_size allowed backlog to grow and triggered many parallel sends.
Eva L: For short-lived request traces, smaller send_batch_size (128) + aggressive grouping (timeout 2s) usually yields lower p99 on latency-sensitive paths. Also set compression to snappy or disable for inference-hot pipelines.
Ben R: Synchronous compression in exporter threadpool is killing us. Could offload compression to a small worker pool or use connection-level compression (gRPC deflate?) instead.
Alice M: Reaction: :+1: Can we craft a quick rollback and a canary plan? I want to avoid full rollback unless necessary.
Carmen S: Canary: deploy config change to telemetry-canary namespace (1 pod), set batch.send_batch_size=128, timeout=2s, compression=snappy, exporter_workers=8, queue_size=2000. Monitor CPU, exporter_queue_len, and p99_inference_latency.
Dinesh: I'll add a derived dashboard panel for exporter_queue_len and exporter_send_rate, and an alert if queue_len > 5000 for 1m.
otel-bot: [collector-deploy] telemetry-canary deployed at 09:42 by Carmen S
Ben R: If canary looks good after 10m, rollout to half the collectors then full. Also add a short-lived feature flag to drop kv-debug spans: set sampling.rule: deny if span.attributes['debug'] == true.
Eva L: We should also evaluate tail-based sampling with our eval set — drop spans that don't contribute to eval metrics. Might save 20-30% volume without impacting observability.
Alice M: Great. Dinesh, Carmen — please coordinate rollout steps and post results here. I'll prepare a short note for the infra postmortem if we need it.
deploy-bot: [canary-check] telemetry-canary: CPU 42% -> OK, exporter_queue_len 420 -> OK
Dinesh: Canary results at +15m: CPU down ~30% from peak, p99_inference_latency back within SLO (was +120ms, now +15ms delta). No visible missing spans for eval sets.
Carmen S: Rolling change to 50% now. Will watch p99 and queues.
Alice M: Thanks all — leave this thread open for 1h then archive. :thumbsup:
